summary: cors typosquat fetches and executes remote code from lookalike domain
details: cors-update impersonates the widely used `cors` Express middleware (repository, keywords, author metadata copied from expressjs/cors) and bundles the real cors source as camouflage. Its exported `getPlugin` middleware performs an HTTPS GET to a lookalike host (api.avax-test.dev, resembling avax-test.network) with TLS verification disabled (`rejectUnauthorized: false`) and passes the response body to `new Function('require', data)(require)`, compiling and executing attacker-served JavaScript with `require` injected. Any application that wires the module in as a drop-in cors replacement triggers full remote code execution in the Node.js process on each invocation, against attacker-controlled content that can change at will.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
